topPRs.title: U19/Karst gas-limit reset reference tasks for all U19 chains
topPRs.author: sbvegan
topPRs.body:
## Context

Karst (U19) has an op-node / kona-node / kona-program bug that leaves each chain's **effective** L2 block gas limit ~55 MGas above the value stored in its `SystemConfig` after the activation block (see Notion *"P/PS: Karst Gas Limit Bug"*). The approved mitigation (option 2b) is a per-chain **SystemConfig transaction** that re-emits the gas `ConfigUpdate`, resetting the effective gas limit back to the on-chain value.

- Sepolia activates **2026-06-17**; Mainnet **2026-07-08**. These tasks run *after* activation on each network.

## What this adds

Reference `SystemConfigGasParams` tasks for the U19 chains (OP, Ink, Metal, Mode, Zora, Soneium, Unichain) on both networks, each re-affirming the chain's **current on-chain gas params** (`gasLimit` re-set to the same value; EIP-1559 params re-affirmed). The template is used **unmodified** — each task is rooted at the chain's real SystemConfig owner via `safeAddressString = "SystemConfigOwner"` (auto-discovered from `SystemConfig.owner()`).

### Mainnet (`src/tasks/eth/`)
| Task | Chain(s) | gasLimit | eip1559 (denom/elast) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `055-gas-params-op` | OP Mainnet | 40M | 250 / 2 |
| `056-gas-params-ink` | Ink | 60M | 250 / 6 | _(calldata-only — see below)_ |
| `057-gas-params-metal-mode` | Metal + Mode (bundled) | 30M | 250 / 6 |
| `058-gas-params-zora` | Zora | 30M | 250 / 6 |
| `059-gas-params-soneium` | Soneium | 40M | 250 / 10 |
| `060-gas-params-unichain` | Unichain | 60M | 250 / 12 |

### Sepolia (`src/tasks/sep/`)
| Task | Chain(s) | gasLimit | eip1559 (denom/elast) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `101-gas-params-op` | OP Sepolia | 40M | 250 / 2 | _(calldata-only — EOA owner)_ |
| `102-gas-params-ink` | Ink Sepolia | 30M | 250 / 6 |
| `103-gas-params-metal-mode-zora` | Metal + Mode + Zora (bundled) | 30M | 250 / 6 |
| `104-gas-params-soneium-minato` | Soneium Minato | 40M | 250 / 10 |
| `105-gas-params-unichain` | Unichain Sepolia | 60M | 50 / 12 |

These SystemConfigs are owned by the **chain operators**, so the tasks are reference artifacts for the operators to execute via their own owner Safe.

## Notes

- **EIP-1559 `(0,0)` chains** (Ink/Metal/Mode/Zora): their SystemConfig getters return `0` because they predate on-chain EIP-1559 config. They run on the genesis/Canyon defaults from the superchain-registry (`denominator = 250`, `elasticity = 6`), confirmed via the L2 block-header `extraData`. The tasks write these explicitly — a behavioral no-op. (`setEIP1559Params(0,0)` would revert with `denominator must be >= 1`, which is why explicit values are used.)
- **Shared-owner bundling**: Metal+Mode (Mainnet) and Metal+Mode+Zora (Sepolia) share one operator Safe and identical params, so they're bundled into one task each.
- **`055-gas-params-op`** is rooted at the Foundation Upgrade Safe (it owns OP Mainnet's SystemConfig); its nonce override is `59` (live + the two nonces consumed by U19 tasks 053/054). Every config carries a "verify the live nonce before signing" note — nonces and captured hashes are point-in-time.
- **Calldata-only tasks**: OP Sepolia's SystemConfig owner is an EOA (no Safe to simulate), and Ink Mainnet's owner Safe has an EIP-7702-delegated signer that trips the simulator's "owner-with-code ⇒ Safe" heuristic (`MultisigTask` calls `nonce()` on it → revert). Both ship as `README.md`-only with the exact `cast` calldata.

## Validation

All 9 full Safe tasks simulate cleanly via `just simulate-stack` (both per-network stacks). The simulator verifies the data-to-sign against each `VALIDATION.md`, so the recorded **Safe Tx / Domain / Message hashes** are confirmed.

## Follow-up (separate PR)

A gas-limit-only template (`SystemConfigGasLimit`) and the EIP-7702 simulator robustness fix are split into their own PRs.

topPRs.title: Ink Sepolia migration tasks (Gelato → OP Enterprise)
topPRs.author: Wazabie
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds the three superchain-ops tasks for the **Ink Sepolia** (`chainId 763373`) rollup-operator migration from **Gelato → OP Enterprise** (Type A Standard OP Stack takeover; cutover **2026-06-22**). Inputs were verified against the _Ink Sepolia Testnet Migration — Engineering Plan_ and cross-checked against live Sepolia state.

| # | Task | Template | Cutover step | Status |
|---|------|----------|--------------|--------|
| 104 | [`ink-sepolia-set-batcher-unsafe-signer`](../tree/af/ink-sepolia-migration/src/tasks/sep/104-ink-sepolia-set-batcher-unsafe-signer) | `SetBatcherAndOrSigner` | 2 & 3 | ✅ simulates; DRAFT |
| 105 | [`ink-sepolia-proposer-rotation`](../tree/af/ink-sepolia-migration/src/tasks/sep/105-ink-sepolia-proposer-rotation) | `SetDisputeGameArgs` | 4 | ✅ simulates; re-sim after U19 |
| 106 | [`ink-sepolia-fee-vault-update`](../tree/af/ink-sepolia-migration/src/tasks/sep/106-ink-sepolia-fee-vault-update) | `FeeVaultUpgradeTemplate` | 15 | ⚠️ **blocked** (see below) |

All three **simulate successfully** on Sepolia (`SIMULATE_WITHOUT_LEDGER=1 just … simulate`). All tasks are **DRAFT, NOT READY TO SIGN**.

## What each task does

### 104 — Set batcher + unsafe block signer
Batches `setBatcherHash` + `setUnsafeBlockSigner` on `SystemConfig` (`0x05C993…bD525`):
- batcher `0x21e57C…002F` (Gelato) → **`0x42c4dBdD6C573b9C2a8657F59EE8E84AE45F2695`** (OPE)
- unsafe signer `0x43ec57…D1a0` (Gelato) → **`0x900C36E0CcAC26F9F49ECa6bbD748e347531864b`** (OPE)

Signed by the **OPE SystemConfig-owner Safe** (`0x837DE4…Fd5E`, 2-of-13). The Gelato→OPE `transferOwnership` is performed off-repo by Gelato (plan step W26); a `SystemConfig.owner()` slot-`0x33` override lets the setters authorize in simulation and **must be removed once W26 lands**.

### 105 — Proposer rotation (proposer-only)
Rotates the **PermissionedDisputeGame** (game type 1) proposer `0xb15d79…4543` (Gelato) → **`0x2282d49d805333D8cd6ddda52B32aC07d6e4e51B`** (OPE) on the DisputeGameFactory (`0x860e62…3D5d`).

Ink's DGF (v1.4.0) uses the **gameArgs blob pattern** (per-chain data lives in `gameArgs(gameType)`, not impl immutables), so `SetDisputeGameArgs` field-diffing is used: only `proposer` is set; **challenger** (`0xfd1d2e…4301`, already the OP Sepolia challenger — OP governance, plan §3.1 "no action") and **prestate** are read live and preserved. Because the prestate is read live, the task is robust to **U19 (2026-06-17)** bumping it — **re-simulate after U19 before signing.** Verified in simulation: the new proposer is set, the old Gelato proposer is fully gone, challenger + prestate unchanged.

### 106 — Fee vault update ⚠️ blocked
Upgrades the 4 fee-vault predeploys to v1.6.0 and re-initializes each recipient via `OptimismPortal2.depositTransaction → L2 ProxyAdmin.upgradeAndCall` (7 deposits). **Two blockers, both documented in the task README/VALIDATION:**

1. **Recipient is a placeholder.** The Kraken fee recipient is an open item in the plan (§1, §3.3 empty placeholder). Current on-chain recipient is the Gelato Safe on L2. `0xdead…00XX` placeholders are used so the state diff is obvious — **replace before signing.**
2. **L2 ProxyAdmin owner = `address(0)`** (verified on-chain, vs. OP Sepolia which returns the aliased L1PAO). The v1.5.0 recipient is immutable, so the change needs a proxy upgrade through the L2 ProxyAdmin — which **reverts on L2** while the owner is unset. **Prerequisite (not in the current plan):** transfer L2 ProxyAdmin ownership to the aliased L1PAO `0x2fc3ff…67f3`. The L1 simulation passes regardless (deposits only emit events on L1) — do not mistake a green L1 sim for a successful L2 effect.

## Verification

- All addresses cross-checked against the migration plan **and** live Sepolia (`SystemConfig`, `DisputeGameFactory.gameArgs(1)`, fee-vault predeploys, safe owners/nonces).
- Domain hashes computed independently and confirmed against the simulation output (104 single-safe; 105/106 nested via the L1PAO = Foundation + Security Council).
- Local simulations succeed for all three (104 produced final domain/message/safe hashes; 105/106 nested message hashes to be regenerated via the nested signing flow before signing).

## Notes for reviewers

- Tasks are numbered **104–106**, following the in-flight `migration-src-0` exercise (101–103) on a separate branch. No directory overlap.
- 105 **must be re-simulated after U19** (2026-06-17); 106 is held until its two blockers are resolved.

topPRs.title: Add SystemConfigGasLimit template (gas-limit-only)
topPRs.author: sbvegan
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Adds **`src/template/SystemConfigGasLimit.sol`** — a minimal `L2TaskBase` template that calls only `SystemConfig.setGasLimit` (no EIP-1559 params). It's the gas-limit-only counterpart to the existing `SystemConfigGasParams`.

## Why

Re-issuing `setGasLimit` re-emits the gas `ConfigUpdate` without touching EIP-1559 params — useful whenever only the gas limit needs to change. The immediate motivation is the **Karst (U19) gas-limit reset**, where re-emitting the `ConfigUpdate` (to clear the post-activation +55 MGas op-node/kona bug) is the *entire* mitigation; the EIP-1559 params are unrelated.

## Details

- Reads `gasParams.gasLimit` from `config.toml` and applies it to each chain in `l2chains`.
- Validates `SystemConfig.gasLimit()` post-execution.
- The gas limit is authorized by the SystemConfig owner, so `safeAddressString` defaults to `"SystemConfigOwner"` (resolved per-chain from `SystemConfig.owner()`); override in `config.toml` if a different root safe is required.
- Does not modify the shared `SystemConfigGasParams` template — fully additive.

## Status / follow-ups

Split out from the U19 gas-reset tasks PR (#1470) so the template can be reviewed independently. No example task / unit test is included yet — happy to add one mirroring `test/tasks/example/eth/006-system-config-gas-params` + the `SystemConfigGasParams` entries in `TaskManager.t.sol` / `Regression.t.sol` if desired before merge.

topPRs.title: docs: complete signing/execution commands in task READMEs + scaffold
topPRs.author: Wazabie
topPRs.body:
## What

Task READMEs `053`/`054` (and the `README.template.md` scaffold) had incomplete signing/execution commands. Restored the full copy-paste flow used by the executed `040`/`041`/`042` tasks — **cd → simulate → sign → approve → execute**, split into *For Signers* / *For Facilitators*.

- Add the `<council|foundation>` safe selector (`053` = 2-of-2, `054` = 3-of-3 incl. `chain-governor`).
- `USE_KEYSTORE=1` is now an optional comment, not hard-coded.
- Add `SKIP_DECODE_AND_PRINT=1` to the sign command — pure speed-up; it only skips the decoded state-diff print, the verified hashes + Tenderly link are unchanged.

Scaffold updated so new tasks are copy-paste-ready out of the box. Executed/cancelled READMEs left as-is.

topPRs.title: fix(MultisigTask): let bare `just execute` work on 1/1 safes (broadcast nonce-bump guardrail)
topPRs.author: Wazabie
topPRs.body:
**Optional guard**, not required fix. The normal way to run tasks `just sign` → `just execute SIGNATURES=...` already works and is unaffected. This just makes a bare `just execute` (no signatures) also work on a **1/1 safe** where today it silently hangs.

It's a safety net, if whoever runs the task forgets to pass `SIGNATURES=...` (easy to do, since nested tasks are run with a bare `just execute`) it just executes correctly instead of silently hanging forever.

## Issue

When you run `just execute` with no signatures, `MultisigTask` does a **simulation only** and it bumps each owner's nonce by 1 to mimic an approval that would happen on-chain. On a **1/1 safe the only owner is the same EOA that's broadcasting the transaction**, so that bump lands on the broadcaster's own nonce. Forge then sends the real transaction at `n+1` and leaves a gap at `n`. Nothing fills `n` so the tx sits **pending forever**.

This only affects a 1/1 EOA safe run with a bare `just execute`:
- **Signed runs** (`SIGNATURES=...`) take a different code path that does do the bump.
- **Nested safes** also run a bare `just execute` (the approvals happen earlier, in `just approve`) but there the bump lands on the child *Safe's* storage, not on the broadcasting EOA, so it's harmless.

## Guard

Skip the simulation-only bump when we're actually broadcasting:

```solidity
if (!_isBroadcastContext()) {
    _incrementOwnerNonce(owners[i]);
}
```

In a real broadcast the bump is faking something that never happens on-chain, so skipping it just lets forge use the true nonce. The transaction still goes through (the signature is valid because the owner *is* the sender). **Simulations are unchanged** they still do the bump, which are needed.

## Testing

- Two regression tests, both fail without the guard: one covers the contract-owner case (`vm.store`), one covers the EOA-owner case (`vm.setNonce` — the one behind the hang).
- Reproduced on a Sepolia fork with the real `migration-src-0` task on the 1/1 ProxyAdminOwner (`0xe934Dc97E347C6aCef74364B50125bb8689c40ff`):

  | | broadcasts at | result |
  |---|---|---|
  | **without guard** | n+1 (4567) | gap at n → hangs forever |
  | **with guard** | n (4566) | mines (block 11073801) → rotation applied → done |
